label: 4th input of sequences starting v ? g (y/f/e/o)
explanation: Extremely sparse (24 activations in 1M sequences), with weak magnitudes (max about 0.13). On dev, 9 of 10 activations are at original step t=3 in sequences of the form v ? g X, where the second token is u/b/k/g and the input X is y, f, e or o (y gives the strongest activations). The one other activation is a copy step (t=10, recalling orig(1)=v) in a sequence starting y v. The predicate t==3 & orig(0)==v & orig(2)==g on its own has 90% recall but only 1.6% precision; restricting the input token to y/f/e/o brings dev precision to 12.5%, and also restricting orig(1) to u/b/k/g gives dev F1 0.9, but that is fit by enumeration on 10 examples. Does not fire on the delimiter or (apart from one case) during copy. There are too few examples to support a general description.
